doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

chapter: Influences and the future of jazz
title: The future of jazz and loss of outlets for young players
summary: He is optimistic but wants more outlets, noting earlier players learned in dances, circuses and movies.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What do you feel about the way jazz is going right now? The future of it, and as someone who’s making their living in jazz, does it bode well do you think?

I think it’s doing wonderful. In fact I think it’s making tremendous progress in more ways than one. You don’t have all the — everything changes, the setting. A lot of the settings have changed you see, especially since the beginnings of jazz. But things are supposed to change. But even in the change, the music itself still flourishes and goes along. And that’s the beautiful part of it. So you don’t have so many of the clubs or the dance halls or stuff. But you have the concert halls. You have the schools. Now the only thing is I would like to see more outlets for the talent. Because you have almost twice as much, many more musicians now.
There’s a lot of young talent out there. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
